A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HiFlow. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v2's appendices A-F. Methods and results can be matched across the reorganization; v1 ends after its references.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation comparisons, quantitative quality metrics, inference latency and component ablations in Section 4, Tables 1-3 and associated figures.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds Diffusion-4k comparisons, qualitative seed comparisons and a failure example in the appendix.

M1.justification: The virtual reference flow and initialization, direction and acceleration alignment procedures remain unchanged. v1's velocity update in Eq. 12 becomes v2's Eq. 13. Appendix A discloses ancillary inference techniques without establishing that they were newly introduced into the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate high-resolution text-to-image generation using the same caption collection and LAION-High-Resolution reference data, with the same broad Flux, SDXL, LoRA, ControlNet and quantization applications. Additional or replaced images remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: Diffusion-4k is added to the 2K and 4K comparisons in Table 1 and to Figure 6. The DALL-E 3 and Flux-Pro qualitative comparisons are removed. UltraPixel, DemoFusion, DiffuseHigh, I-Max and Flux plus BSRGAN remain.

E3.justification: Qualitative inputs and configurations change: Figure 5 replaces the man-and-camel example with an elf, and SVDQuant illustrations include 2048-square outputs instead of the earlier 1440-square outputs. Figure F.9 introduces a controlled two-prompt, three-seed comparison. The main 30-step, 1K-caption and 10K-reference-image protocol is retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds a qualitative seed-variation check in Figure F.9 and a duplicated-tail failure case in Figure E.2. The FID diagnostic drops the curves labelled sampling steps 10 and 15, retaining the final-sample comparison. Component-ablation scores remain unchanged, although the 4K visual example is replaced.

E5.justification: Appendix B and Figure F.9 first explicitly report seeds 0, 1 and 2 for two 4K prompts. This adds qualitative variation reporting, but neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run uncertainty for the benchmark scores.

E6.justification: All retained Table 1 scores and Tables 2-3 values are unchanged. New Diffusion-4k rows report FID 60.96 at 2K and 77.95 at 4K. Qualitative results are added or replaced, including seed and failure examples, while commercial-model examples and two diagnostic FID curves disappear. No same-setting HiFlow score improvement is reported.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds a differential formulation relating acceleration to the derivative of the predicted clean sample. Its discrete Eq. 17 uses a factor of -1/t_i, whereas Eq. 10 in both versions uses -1/t_{i-1}. This introduces a limited mathematical inconsistency; the main derivation and update rule are retained.

C1.justification: The introduction changes the claim of comparability with UltraPixel and commercial models into a claim of better performance than UltraPixel and Diffusion-4k. Section 4.2 similarly strengthens this comparison. The central training-free, model-agnostic framework and three alignment contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix D elaborates acceleration as the model's detail-synthesis rhythm and connects alignment to classifier-free guidance. Appendix E grounds the existing reference-quality limitation in a duplicated-tail example. Section 3.2 also introduces an incorrect interpretation: it says discrepancy increases as t approaches zero, while Figure 3(a) shows it decreasing to zero.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly names NTK-aware RoPE scaling, attention-entropy balancing and image/text sequence balancing; Tables F.1-F.3 provide generation prompts. Conversely, v1's guidance scales of 4.5 for 2K and 7.5 for 4K are omitted. The first-page repository pointer becomes a project-page pointer. These are documentation changes, not evidence of reruns.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on recent high-resolution generation, inference scaling and quantization, and acknowledges FireFlow's use of acceleration. DALL-E 3, Flux-Pro and Voxurf references disappear. The discussion emphasizes distribution mismatch and missing detail guidance more explicitly, while retaining the same broad research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and motivation are expanded, contribution bullets become an inline enumeration, and terminology and method explanations receive local edits. The main section sequence remains stable. Limitations move from Section 4.5 to Appendix E, within a newly organized supplement.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially revised: the opening gallery is largely replaced, Figure 2 is compressed, the FID plot is redrawn, and Figures 6 and 8 are rebuilt. The appendix adds galleries, seed and failure panels, and prompt tables. Some existing images and acceleration visualizations are relocated or enlarged rather than newly produced.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves empirical support and transparency through the Diffusion-4k comparison, disclosed inference techniques and prompts, and explicit seed and failure examples. These benefits outweigh localized regressions: omitted guidance-scale settings, the reversed FID-trend statement in Section 3.2, and the inconsistency between Eqs. 17 and 10. The retained core results and limited additional validation support a modest overall gain.
